english.note: Use 功夫 when you specifically mean Chinese kung fu or martial-arts skill, rather than a named non-Chinese discipline.

examples.english: I learned a Chinese martial art from Master Lee when I was young, and I still practise every day.
examples.traditional: 我細個跟李師傅學過功夫，依家仲日日練。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 sai3 go3 gan1 lei5 si1 fu2 hok6 gwo3 gung1 fu1 ji1 gaa1 zung6 jat6 jat6 lin6

english.note: Use this everyday noun for the effort or work put into getting something done.
Use this for effort invested in getting something done, rather than physical force.
Use 功夫 for the effort or labour put into accomplishing a particular task.

examples.english: We put a lot of graft into making this model.
examples.traditional: 整呢個模型真係落咗好多功夫。
examples.jyutping: zing2 ni1 go3 mou4 jing4 zan1 hai6 lok6 zo2 hou2 do1 gung1 fu1

examples.english: I had to push hard to get this report right.
examples.traditional: 為咗整好呢份報告，我落咗好多功夫。
examples.jyutping: wai6 zo2 zing2 hou2 ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3 ngo5 lok6 zo2 hou2 do1 gung1 fu1

examples.english: We put a lot of work into this report.
examples.traditional: 呢份報告落咗好多功夫。
